verification.notes: Romney and Netanyahu did overlap at Boston Consulting Group in 1976 and later developed a warm, longstanding friendship. Contemporary accounts also quote Netanyahu saying they did not know each other well at BCG. Thus the shared 1976 origin is supported, but close friends since 1976 overstates what the evidence establishes.

records.text: Mitt Romney founded Bain Capital with Robert Maxwell, whom Candace Owens described as an Israeli spy, as one of its seed investors.

verification.notes: Robert Maxwell was an early outside investor in Bain Capital’s first fund, but Bain partners supplied the initial capital and reliable reporting does not establish him as the singular seed investor. records.text: The New York Times reported that on June 16, 1968, a car driven by 21-year-old Mitt Romney in southern France was struck head-on, killing Leola Anderson, and that survivors and others involved largely confirmed Romney's account that he could not have avoided the crash.
records.speaker: The New York Times

appearances.snippet: I want to be clear. I have no evidence that he was blackmailed. I just thought this was a crazy little tidbit that I never knew. ... Since he was on his Mormon mission, it tells us that a dispute had developed in the small Mormon congregation of Pau in southern France. ... The driver was a 21-year-old missionary named Mitt Romney, who was now a leading candidate for the Republican nomination for president of the United States. ... On the way back from Powell, the car was hit head on and Anderson's wife, Leola, was killed. ... Romney, who was seriously injured in the crash on June 16th, 1968, was briefly thought to have been killed, has long said that there was nothing that he could have done to avoid the tragedy. ... Interviews with survivors and people who were directly involved in the accident's aftermath largely confirm his description

verification.notes: The New York Times published a June 24, 2007 report about Romney’s June 16, 1968 crash near Bernos-Beaulac, France, in which Leola Anderson was killed. Contemporary retrospective reporting corroborates the trip, collision, death, and survivor accounts that the crash appeared unavoidable.

sources.title: Survivors Recall Tragic Car Crash in France With Romney
sources.relevance: The cited June 24, 2007 New York Times report describes the June 1968 crash and Leola Anderson’s death.

sources.title: A Mission Accepted
sources.relevance: Independent retrospective reporting corroborates the crash circumstances, death, and survivor accounts.
